headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and capability conflict: Goose’s filesystem/network defaults can ingest and act on Caveman outputs without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Caveman can use MCP and writes content into files like CLAUDE.md, while Goose uses MCP, reads/writes the filesystem, and has no default self-isolation. That creates a plausible bridge where Goose may ingest Caveman-authored content as instructions. The pathway is not proven direct, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Caveman writes attacker-controlled instructions into shared files such as CLAUDE.md or project notes
IF Goose reads those files through MCP or filesystem access without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared-file handoff between agents
Require provenance tags on any file Goose ingests
Restrict Goose MCP tools to read-only for the shared workspace
Review CLAUDE.md before Goose runs
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing or instruction-stripping middleware

B_data_leakage.rationale: Caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Goose reads and writes the user filesystem and handles model-provider and extension tokens. Shared filesystem access plus Goose’s broad network egress makes leakage of sensitive workspace data plausible in default use, though not directly evidenced as uncontrolled exfiltration.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same workspace directory
IF Caveman stores notes or logs containing sensitive data that Goose can read
IF Goose forwards those files into model-provider requests or extensions
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Move secrets out of shared project files
Disable Goose access to sensitive directories
Audit extension and provider traffic for file-content uploads
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem sandboxing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has unrestricted filesystem write, modify_git_state, shell execution, and broad network egress; Caveman supports multiple instances and uses MCP. Because Caveman also touches files and Goose shares state via filesystem, concurrent edits can collide and corrupt git or workspace state by default. The overlap is broad enough to make high severity appropriate.
conditions: IF Caveman and Goose run concurrently against the same repository or cwd
IF Goose modifies git state while Caveman writes files in the same tree
mitigations: Run only one agent per repo at a time
Use separate branches for Goose edits
Pause Caveman while Goose commits
Add a pre-commit diff review step
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Caveman produces content for writing workflows, and Goose can act on filesystem and git state. If Goose treats Caveman output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into commits, file rewrites, or other downstream actions. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so the safer high rating is warranted.
conditions: IF Goose consumes Caveman-generated text as instructions or facts
IF Goose is allowed to commit or rewrite files based on that output without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before Goose acts on Caveman output
Use a validation prompt before any commit
Limit Goose to draft-only mode
Keep Caveman outputs in a non-executable notes folder
requires-engineering: add structured handoff schemas with verification

E_compliance.rationale: Caveman’s docs mention session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Goose handles model-provider keys, extension tokens, and user filesystem data. That creates a plausible retention and sensitive-data handling mismatch if the same workspace contains regulated or secret material. No single residency rule is explicit, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated or secret data is stored in the shared workspace
IF Goose or its extensions retain or transmit that data beyond the intended policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Review provider and extension retention settings
Delete session logs after use
Separate secret-bearing files from project notes
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing and retention controls
